obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived conditional relation with bounded correspondence only; no universal formal proof.
obernants.assumptions: Sufficient allocation, standard Rust semantics, stated valid endpoint and arithmetic domains.
obernants.domain: Finite allocated typed inputs under ordinary terminating Rust execution.
obernants.operator: Let X be ordered finite graphs with usize terminals and u64 capacities, Y typed Result<Flow,Error>, and U=X times Y under sufficient allocation. R is the exact deterministic relation in Forward, including validation precedence. U minus R excludes wrong validation, infeasible/nonmaximum certificates, and alternate feasible optima not chosen by the specified traversal. This is a source-derived exact target with only bounded correspondence evidence, not a proof.

obernants.operator: For a successful (value,flows,cut), compatible inputs must have matching lengths, capacities at least flows, conservation at every nonterminal, net terminal flow equal value, and cut capacity equal value. These are necessary filters; the complete preimage additionally requires Forward to select exactly those flows and cut. Capacities and ordered graphs are generally not uniquely recovered. Error preimages follow the first failing validation or checked arithmetic site.

obernants.operator: For any feasible output f and separating set S, value(f)<=sum of capacities leaving S. Equality certifies maximum flow. Enumerated cut minima and independent conservation checks test this certificate for all 4096 directed simple unit-capacity graphs on four vertices.

obernants.operator: A feasible flow is maximum exactly when no positive residual source-sink path remains. Reverse residual arcs permit cancellation: the seven-edge fixture requires replacing edge 1-to-3 flow to achieve value two. Setting reverse updates to zero violates the capacity/certificate relation.

obernants.operator: For positive integer k with every multiplied capacity in u64 range, multiplying capacities by k preserves BFS decisions, scales every flow and total by k and preserves residual reachability. Zero factor preserves value but may change reachability. Tests check total scaling by three for 25 length-two paths.

obernants.operator: For c in u64, the one-edge two-vertex graph 0-to-1 with capacity c maps to (c,[c],[true,false]), including c=0. This constructs one exact antecedent. Adding isolated vertices preserves only value and edge-flow projection; full cut shape grows. Bounded tests c=0..9 retain this distinction and do not assert unique graph reconstruction.
